prompt:
The frame is back up after dismantling and the survey team is recording the front elevation.

Already fixed and not yours to move: the hall is five bays wide and its front columns are numbered at the base, C1 to C5, with C3 the middle one; a taut line is strung under the eaves from end to end and it is dead level; a plumb bob hangs on its cord in front of the middle bay and is still; a light scaffold stands at one end. The team is standing square in front of the hall.

What the conservation specification for this hall says:
the columns of the front are set leaning towards the middle of the front rather than standing plumb, and the further from the middle a column stands the more it leans;
the middle column stands plumb;
the column heads climb away from the middle towards both ends of the front, so the eaves line is a shallow curve rather than a straight line, and the end columns stand highest.

How far each column ends up off the plumb line and where each head ends up against the taut line is the part I am deliberately not telling you, and no drawing of the elevation is in the picture to copy. Nothing is written on the frame beyond the base labels.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show the front of a traditional timber building with a row of columns under a wide eaves? A photo, an illustration, a schematic or a plain diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows a blank card stating an answer with no building in it, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.head_scale: clearly above the taut line|just above the taut line|level with the taut line
reference.lean_state: C1=leans towards the middle|C2=leans towards the middle|C3=stands plumb|C4=leans towards the middle|C5=leans towards the middle

steps.target: a numbered column base with its own column and the eaves above it

steps.read_crop: In this cut-out, what label is on the column base? Answer with the label exactly as it is written, or none if no label is on it.

In this cut-out, where is the top of this column against the taut line strung under the eaves? Answer with one of: clearly above the taut line, just above the taut line, level with the taut line, or none if the taut line cannot be made out.

steps.target: a numbered column base with its own column and the eaves above it

steps.read_crop: In this cut-out, what label is on the column base? Answer with the label exactly as it is written, or none if no label is on it.

In this cut-out, how does the column stand: does it lean towards the left edge of the picture, lean towards the right edge of the picture, or stand straight up and down? Answer with one of: leans left, leans right, stands plumb, or none if the column cannot be made out.

steps.target: a numbered column base with its own column and the eaves above it

steps.read_crop: In this cut-out, is a label written on the column base? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: a written word or drawn line on the frame beyond the base labels
